sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Broad-leaved pepperweed is a rhizomatous perennial from Eurasia, often found in wet, saline or disturbed soils. Its flowering stems reach about 1–2 m; it has become invasive in several parts of North America.

sections.title: Leaves and fruit
sections.text: Large basal leaves contrast with smaller upper leaves. Tiny white flowers form branched panicles. The fruits are two-chambered silicles, each usually containing a seed about 1 mm long.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No adequately documented food use is included here. The plant spreads through deep rhizomes, so avoid spreading it while harvesting.
